title: Cohort escrow + pin backoff: safe canary routing and graceful variant fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a routing safety layer that combines cohort-based canary assignments with an escrowed pin TTL and exponential pin backoff to reduce unsafe exposures during model version rollouts. This ticket defines the algorithm, edge behaviors, and operational guardrails for: 1) cohort escrow windows used to delay permanent session pinning until canary health signals stabilize; 2) pin backoff that progressively relaxes version affinity when downstream variants degrade; and 3) deterministic fallback ordering across region/tier/model-variant dimensions.
implementation_notes: Introduce a short-lived 'escrow' state for newly-allocated pins: requests initially assigned to canary cohort become escrowed for X minutes before converting to full session pins
Escrow time defaults to 5 minutes; configurable per rollout and shortened when canary traffic exceeds 10% and latency/error signals are stable
Pin record schema: <session_id, cohort_id, variant_id, state=escrow|active, created_ts, ttl_ms, backoff_level>

Backoff behavior: when a variant in active pin state shows a degradation (error-rate jump or P95 latency spike beyond thresholds), increment backoff_level and shorten TTL by backoff factor; at backoff_level threshold, convert pin to probabilistic routing with retention decay
Routing precedence: region affinity -> tier preference -> cohort/variant pin. Fallbacks evaluate by cost/latency compatibility matrix and operator-defined safety tiers
Telemetry: expose a pin lifecycle metric (escrow_created, escrow_promoted, backoff_triggered, pin_expired) and tag with rollout_id and cohort label
Make the mechanism compatible with existing session-anchoring and shard-pinning proto changes in ENG-13012 and ENG-62100
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for escrow->active transition and TTL/backoff arithmetic
Integration test that simulates a canary with injected latency/errors and verifies backoff causes pins to decay instead of sticking
E2E scenario: region failover while cohort pins exist must still route requests to fallback variant within target SLOs
Dashboard charting pin state counts and backoff events, and an alert when backoff events exceed 1% of canary traffic over 15m
Performance: adding escrow metadata to routing lookup should not increase median routing latency by >1ms at 99th percentile under realistic QPS
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature flag gated rollout in staging with synthetic canary traffic (1 day)
Stage 1: Internal canary enabled for 5% of production traffic in a single region (48 hours), observe backoff and pin metrics
Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 25% across multiple geo-tiers with operator supervision and automatic rollback hook if backoff rate > 3% and customer-facing errors increase
Stage 3: GA enablement with configurable defaults and runtime knobs in Console; publish runbook and post-mortem template
monitoring_signals: fallback_success_rate (requests that hit fallback within single RTT budget)
steps: 1) Finalize escrow TTL semantics and backoff multipliers with PM and SRE
2) Implement pin state machine and DB schema updates in routing service
3) Wire telemetry and lightweight traces for pin handoffs
4) Create console controls for rollout-id and escrow TTL overrides
5) Run chaos tests that simulate region latency spikes and verify graceful degrade
6) Gradual deployment controlled by feature flag and rollout job

decision: Adopt escrow-first pinning with configurable TTL and exponential backoff. Default escrow=5m, base TTL=1h, backoff multiplier=0.5 per backoff_level, probabilistic degrade after 3 backoffs.
